newsitem.title: USA: Gillette/Duracell deal would be good fit -analysts.
newsitem.headline: Gillette/Duracell deal would be good fit -analysts.

text.p: A merger expected to be announced shortly between Gillette Co and Duracell International Inc would be a good fit, analysts said.
Sources familiar with the situation said the $7 billion deal would involve a stock swap.
The merger would be "a real good deal" for Gillette, said Bear Stearns & Co analyst Constance Maneaty.
"It meets all the acquisition criteria (Gillette Chief Executive Officer) Al Zeien set," said Maneaty in a telephone interview. She said that if the deal were as reported, "It's a perfect fit."

Goldman Sachs analyst Amy Low agreed "It's a very good deal. It meets every criteria...including a global brand with a number one position, room for international expansion, high margins and significant synergies, particularly in the distribution and sales force levels."
Maneaty noted Duracell is a worldwide leader in alkaline batteries and has been very profitable, showing a high unit growth. "I can't find anything wrong with it," Maneaty said of the transaction.

Under the deal, each Duracell share would be valued at 0.904 share of Gillette, or $58.85 per share, said sources familiar with the situation. "If that's the price," Maneaty said, "then it's not too high. It's really a very fair price."

Moody's Investors Service analyst Joseph Chakra, who declined to discuss the merger, noted that the rating agency's current rating on Gillette's long-term debt was AA3 and it had the highest rating, Prime-1, for its commercial paper program.

Duracell, which has not issued any long-term debt, had its commerial paper program recently upgraded to Prime-1. "The rating basically reflects its good presence in the market and its international presence. There is an increase in the use of batteries -- any advancement in electronics is good for battery companies," Chakra said.
